open_differences.what: the front stack's height: the print's cap stands about 167 px (about 3.5 m) over the cresting beside it, its top at y 128 px; the build holds it to 18.0 m, the most the c. 1895 Taylor print allows (it shows nothing over the deck there), so its cap renders well under the print's (L-kimball-1801-south-stacks-3107)

the stacks' heads: a moulded collar (about y 200-220 px on the front one) under a stage of diamond-latticed panels about 1.5 m deep and a moulded cap, the stage about 0.15 m proud of the shaft each side; the build lays one plain cap 0.8 m deep (T-3109)

the stacks' lower stages: each shaft widens below about the curb into a broader base carried down the steep lower face to the cornice (the front one x 860-965 px below y 350); the build's shafts run straight (T-3109)

the south cornice, re-measured on the rebuilt corner through the re-solved camera (T-3108; it read about 85 px under the print's at the corner): the round's wall top renders about 19 px under the print's (y 614 against 595) and its balustrade's rail about 50 px under (y 560 against 510), and the main cornice at the south-east corner about 23 px over (y 632 against 655). The pavilion's window rows fit within about 13 px; the round's rows read about 20 px under the print's, so through this camera the round's storeys stand about 0.3 m higher than the build's against the pavilion's, which the Taylor print (it sees only the round's cornice end) cannot check

the light behind the corner balcony: a small window on the canted face over the round bay (x 640-680, y 445-500); the build's chamfer face is blank there (T-3108 tried K08's sash on the cant and its recess rendered occluded, so it was taken out)

the front north of the pavilion: the camera re-solved on the rebuilt corner (T-3108) cannot also fit the loggia: its arch's crown renders about 117 px north of the print's (x 278 against 395) and the bow between them wider than the print's, where T-3107's camera, fitted with the pavilion's face free to stand 2.1 m proud, held the arch within 10 px. The front's layout between the loggia and the pavilion and this picture's do not agree; the Taylor camera holds that stretch

the south bay: the print's bay toward the east end (its front x about 1000-1150 px, its canted east side x 1150-1222 in shade) stands proud of the wall, the 1911 sheet's 0.8 m projection over u 12.1-6.7 with canted sides; the build's south wall is flat (T-3109)

the south wall's openings: the print shows one column at x 850-905 px near the round bay and one on the bay's front at x 1060-1125 (second-storey sill about y 835, transom at y 755), with the tree hiding the wall between; the build's three reconstructed columns at u 6.5, 11.5 and 16.5, two of which fall on the print's two (T-3109)

the south mansard's dormers: a hooded dormer between the stacks (x 1040-1130 px, its light y 430-490, a tall slated hood over it) and a small light behind the corner balcony (x 640-680); the build has none on this face (T-3109)
the roof's south-east corner: a tall slender pinnacle or gablet (x 1200-1245 px, y 380-600) where the south slope meets the rear; the build has none (T-3109)

the recessed range behind the south-east corner: set back from the wall, tall glazed openings under a carved head at about the cornice (x 1225-1300 px, y 610-770); the build's rear wings stand there plain (T-3109)
the rear range beyond the court: a lower two-storey white range with a gable and a hooded dormer facing the court (x 1300-1640 px); the build's wings stand there with hipped roofs (T-3110)
the tower's form: a shaft about 2.4 m across under a corbelled upper stage about 3.6 m across, its cone flaring from the stage; the build is one eight-sided prism 2.9 m across

the flank section stands about 0.1 m proud on the sheet; the build stands it 0.6 m proud (K08's pavilion depth, the least its window recesses fit in; the main eave's gutter, its lip 0.46 m out, also dies behind it). Its width is ruled with it (T-3001): at the built depth the build's 6.0 m (u 5.1-11.1) renders its west edge at about x 500 against the print's pilaster at x 497-501, so T-2538's 7.8 m was its camera's; at the sheet's 0.1 m the same edge falls at u 3.9 and the section would be about 7.2 m, so moving it to the sheet's depth means widening it past K08's 6.0 m. The pavilion stood 0.6 m proud too
open_differences.how: L-kimball-1801-k01-2843; T-3001 the flank section's. The pavilion's is fixed: T-3047 stands it 0.1 m proud as a shallow projection, its recesses run back through the wall plane, its gable a parapet carried back past it, and the mansard's eave box and gutter stopped at its cheeks (L-kimball-1801-pavilion-shallow-3047)

open_differences.what: the east turret's shaft and finial: the print shows the shaft about 15 px wider toward the front (to x 237; the build's to about x 220), a moulded band at its first floor and a heavy eave moulding, and a finial spike about 2.5 m tall over the cone's neck (y 778 to 702), where the build's stands about 0.7 m
open_differences.how: Its pixel figures were read through T-2538's camera; T-3060's re-solved camera moves the front's north-west corner about 25 px west and the far flank about 25 px east, so re-read them before working it. T-3074 re-solved it again (the horizon on the lake line, about 30 px higher), so read them through the current camera.

open_differences.what: the mansard's curb and deck: at the front's north-west corner the print's curb stands about 35-50 px lower than the build's (the corner hip's top at about x 950, y 320 against 978, 247) and its corner hip runs about 25-30 px west of the build's; the front's deck ends at the print's x 1092 under its south finial, where the build's runs on to x 1187. So the cresting, the corner hood and its finial stand about 35-50 px over the print's, and the south finial about 95 px south of it (seen by T-3000)
open_differences.how: T-1890 (its T-3000 finding). Its pixel figures were read through T-2538's camera; T-3060's re-solved camera moves the front's north-west corner about 25 px west and the far flank about 25 px east, so re-read them before working it. T-3074 re-solved it again (the horizon on the lake line, about 30 px higher), so read them through the current camera.

open_differences.what: the hooded dormers' hoods: the print's cheeks widen further up the roof than the build's (the flank's lit cheek about 45 px across at the top against the build's about 25), as its lower faces fall back faster than the build's 72 degrees do; and their faces are slate with a pale frame round the light, where the build's are stone
open_differences.how: T-1890 (with the curb; seen by T-3000). Its pixel figures were read through T-2538's camera; T-3060's re-solved camera moves the front's north-west corner about 25 px west and the far flank about 25 px east, so re-read them before working it. T-3074 re-solved it again (the horizon on the lake line, about 30 px higher), so read them through the current camera.

open_differences.what: the gabled section's openings: the print's principal storey has three round-arched lights across the section (x 360-440), the second an oriel on corbels with a carved panel over it (x 362-435, about 5.4-8.1 m), and the third an open loggia behind the balustrade (x 382-422, its head about 11.4 m) under the gable; the build lays one mullioned and transomed pair a storey on the pavilion and its balustrade bows out where the print's runs straight; the print's pier at about u 0-0.9 (x 422-445), up to the cornice, is not built

the flank section's top: over the corbel table (about 9.5 m) the print's section carries a third storey of paired lights under a cornice, a gabled wall dormer with a finial (x 520-600) and the tall round-topped stack (x 467-530); the build carries the section's wall to 13.9 m under K08's low hip

the lights over the loggia, on the front and the flank: the print's outlines read about 1.4 m across (x 1016-1071 and 877-931 px), about 1.2 m once the lit reveal of the near jamb is taken off, against the build's 1.15 m (K01's widest ordinary sash); their transom bar stands about 0.75-1.0 m under the head where K06's transom light is 0.45 m; and each stands in a moulded frame under a projecting head between carved pilasters, where the build lays K01's flat arch

photo2_library_record.title: 2. Historic American Buildings Survey Harold Allen, Photographer , June 1965 VIEW: EXTERIOR - FROM NW, NORTH (18th ST.) AND WEST (PRAIRIE AVE.) ELEVATIONS - W. W. Kimball House, 1801 South Prairie Avenue, Chicago, Cook County, IL
photo2_library_record.camera_position: from the northwest corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street
photo2_library_record.creator: Harold Allen for HABS
photo2_library_record.repository: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Division
photo2_library_record.rights_basis: HABS photograph made for the U.S. Government; LoC: no known restrictions on publication
photo2_library_record.notes: North (18th Street) and west (Prairie Avenue) elevations from the north-west: corner tower, conical and hipped slate roofs, dormers, the long 18th Street side running east with its service/stable end. Utility poles and wires are 1965 intrusions. Best single view for massing of the 1801 corner as it stood in 1904 (house complete 1892; Kimball died 1904, widow lived here to 1921).

grade.why: Pictured: 9 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

placement.position_note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin, kept (lot frame u 18.000, v -11.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.454 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south from the 18th Street wall and the Taylor camera, solved in this frame, stands unchanged (T-2843).
placement.symbolic_location: 1801 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1801 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's two rectangles behind the main block, in the trace's own lines (T-2843), with the walls and roofs the Taylor photograph shows on the 18th Street flank. r3: the gabled section, u -4.6 to 0 and v 0 to 6.0 where the trace's south line steps in (the draft's fit stood it 0.5 m off the 18th Street wall, which the trace and the photograph run straight). T-3001, read through T-3074's camera on the 18th Street wall's plane: the photograph's section runs from about u -4.5 (its principal storey's round-arched lights and the oriel over them) to its pier at about u +0.9, three storeys to a cornice at about 11.7 m, so it stands on the main block's rear wall from u -4.6 (it ran the trace's whole rectangle to u -8.5 at 13.9 m, where the print shows sky above about 8.4 m); three storeys (3.55, 3.1 and 3.6 m) to 11.7 m under a 45-degree slate hip, its eave pulled in to 0.05 m so it stays behind its pavilion's face; its 18th Street face carries the coped gable and balcony as a shallow K08 pavilion (bays.p_gable), and where it stands past the main block's 8.1 m wall top under a ridge along it, its own front closes the junction (L-kimball-1801-gabled-section-3001). r3b: the rest of the trace's rectangle, u -8.5 to -4.6 and v 0 to 6.0, built at the east range's two storeys to 6.35 m under a 45-degree slate hip (the tree hides it on the print; the range's roof rises to the section there), one light on its 18th Street wall at a reconstructed place. r2: the east range, two storeys to 6.35 m under a 45-degree slate hip (T-3076, read through T-3074's camera at the wall's depth: its sill course about 1.2-1.4 m, its first storey's lights about 1.35-2.8 m, the band under its upper storey 4.15 m and its eaves about 6.2-6.4 m, so its floor is laid at 0.75 m, 0.7 m under the main block's, for lights 0.6 m over it; T-2538's 8.1-8.2 m was read through a camera whose flank receded too steeply), from u -8.5 back to the trace's rear at u -17.9, where the camera's bearing also puts the flank's east end (the draft's fit stopped at u -17.0). T-2900 runs it the trace's whole length, v 0 to 18.3 (the trace's south face at y -3235.6 to -3235.7, its front at x 1448.7-1448.8 from v 6.0 on), as a K01 wing longer than its host wall (past_host): it stands on r3b's 6 m rear wall and past it has a front wall of its own, and its 45-degree slate hip runs along it, ridge about 12.8 m, its eaves carried round the front where it runs past the gabled section. Its north-east turret is a K08 corner turret on its 18th Street wall (bays.turret). Openings are the kit's sash at reconstructed places: three on the 18th Street wall clear of the turret, three on the rear, two on the south face and three on the front's free stretch; no picture shows the rear, the south face or the front.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall south of the gabled section, which no picture shows.
